name: Hawaiʻi Conservation Program
summary: Annual NFWF grants in Hawaiʻi for endemic forest bird recovery, including predator and ungulate control, fencing, mosquito suppression and native plant outplanting.
reporting: Grantees pick the metrics that fit their project from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system, such as miles of fencing maintained, animals removed and birds released.

deadline.text: October 21, 2026 by 5:59 PM Hawaiʻi Standard Time

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date - Wednesday, October 21, 2026 by 5:59 PM Hawaiʻi Standard Time

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and Organizations, educational institutions, and businesses.

geography.quote: To be eligible for funding, projects must occur within the priority geographic areas illustrated in Maps 1-3 for the focal species located on Hawaiʻi Island, Maui, and Oʻahu

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

window.quote: Full Proposal Due Date - Wednesday, October 21, 2026 by 5:59 PM Hawaiʻi Standard Time

amount.quote: Grant awards generally range in size from $50,000 to $200,000, although grants greater than $200,000 will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

co_finance_required.quote: Projects must have a minimum match of 1:1 federal and/or non-federal cash and/or in-kind contributions.

reporting.quote: the Hawaiʻi Conservation Program has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting
